notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (productivity) team building in-app AI features (smart composer, search, support). Started on Hosted API to iterate quickly; after pilot they want Dedicated for predictable latency and unit economics. Key drivers: lower per-token cost for heavy reranking, predictable throughput for synchronous UX, stronger isolation and control for customer data.

User quotes / call snippets:
- "Latency needs to feel instant to users — p95 < 150ms or feature is dead to PMs" (Head of Product, J. Ramirez).
- "We like the built-in batching and KV caching ideas; can we get tuning knobs exposed in Dedicated?" (Staff ML Engineer).

Technical/POC notes:
- Workload mix: 60% short-turn chat/autocomplete, 30% embeddings/reranking for search, 10% long-form summarization.
- Target throughput: sustained 8–12 req/s per region for peak pages; burst to 30req/s for campaign spikes.
- Acceptable latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms for interactive flows.
- Data handling: customer documents stored in their own S3; inference must avoid persisting PII in platform logs and must support KMS for key management.

Commercial/legal priorities:
- Prefers 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly true-ups. Wants clear failure/fallback policy to Hosted if Dedicated capacity constrained.
- MSA redlines focus on IP assignment for derivative model outputs, indemnity limits, and a mutual confidentiality clause.
- SLA needs: 99.95% availability, p95 latency SLO for dedicated pool, and service credits defined for breaches.

Security/vendor onboarding:
